title.rendered: The Wisdom That Comes From Above: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: The wisdom that comes from above is first pure, then peace-loving, considerate, submissive, full of mercy and good fruit, impartial and sincere. Two wisdoms compete for your decisions.

content.rendered:
The wisdom that comes from above is first pure, then peace-loving, considerate, submissive, full of mercy and good fruit, impartial and sincere. Two wisdoms compete for your decisions. Only one comes from God.

The Gospel For Today | Monday, June 22, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“But the wisdom that comes from heaven is first of all pure; then peace-loving, considerate, submissive, full of mercy and good fruit, impartial and sincere.”
James 3:17 (NIV)

Today’s Message

James writes one of the most practical letters in the New Testament. He is a pastor. He is watching his people live. And in chapter three, he names something most believers know but rarely articulate. There are two kinds of wisdom available. One comes from above. One does not. Both will sound reasonable in the moment. Only one bears the fruit of God.

The wisdom that does not come from above, James says, is “earthly, unspiritual, demonic.” It looks like wisdom. It often makes a lot of strategic sense. It is the wisdom that protects the self at the cost of others. The wisdom that wins arguments at the cost of love. The wisdom that climbs ladders at the cost of integrity. The wisdom that justifies cruelty by calling it candour. The wisdom that calls bitterness honest and self-promotion ambition. It is everywhere in modern culture. It runs many boardrooms. It dominates many social media feeds. And it has crept, more than the church wants to admit, into many ministries.

The wisdom that comes from above has a different fingerprint. James names seven marks. Pure first. Then peace-loving. Considerate. Submissive. Full of mercy and good fruit. Impartial. Sincere. Notice the order. Purity comes first because no other mark stands without it. A wisdom that is peaceful but not pure can be cowardice. A wisdom that is merciful but not pure can be enabling. The wisdom of God starts with rightness before God. From that root, everything else grows.

For the believer making decisions today, James gives a simple test. The wisdom in front of you wants to be acted on. Before you act on it, hold it up against the seven marks. Is it pure? Does it move toward peace? Is it considerate of others, especially those with less power than you? Is it willing to submit to wise counsel? Is it full of mercy? Does it produce good fruit? Is it impartial, not favouring one person over another? Is it sincere, not hiding ulterior motives?

If the wisdom you are about to follow fails the test, it is the other wisdom. Drop it. If it passes, walk in it. The believer who trains themselves to make decisions by James’s seven-mark test slowly becomes a person whose judgement can be trusted by everyone around them. Not because they are clever. Because they have learned to recognise the voice from above.

Prayer

Father, give me Your wisdom today. Pure first. Then peace-loving, considerate, submissive, full of mercy and good fruit, impartial and sincere. Help me recognise the earthly wisdom that often sounds so reasonable, and refuse it. Train my judgement until the wisdom from above is the only wisdom my heart accepts. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

I walk in the wisdom that comes from above. My decisions today are pure, peace-loving, considerate, submissive, full of mercy and good fruit, impartial and sincere. I refuse earthly wisdom no matter how reasonable it sounds. The wisdom of God is my counsellor.
